title: What Belongs in the Tool and Which Behaviour Must Be Taught:
text:
What Belongs in the Tool and Which Behaviour Must Be Taught:.    Educating   the mind   in a health ecosystem saturated with AI:   What belongs in the tool,   and which behaviour must be taught on the job   
  edited by Angelo Rossi Mori, IRPPS-CNR;   produced with Claude.ai, following the augmented-reasoning approach        
   
   What to teach and what to build into the AI tool,   for five differentiated groups of actors     
 When AI systems in health and social care become genuinely reliable, the educational problem does not shrink: it changes shape and becomes harder. The entry-level work through which competence used to form is precisely the work these systems absorb first, so the loss falls on the apprenticeship rather than on expert performance, and it stays invisible until the moment someone has to work without the system.   
 This document separates what can be made invariant, and therefore belongs inside the tool, from what cannot, and therefore has to be learned on the job. The separation runs down four levels nested one inside the other. The first is the disposition of the generalist model itself — asking before answering, declaring what it has assumed, never reassuring about what cannot be excluded — which must already be there before any content is loaded. The second is a reference configuration for the domain, ideally produced as a public good and agreed by authoritative national or international bodies. The third is the local customisation of the individual instance. The fourth is the knowledge base loaded into it. The descent can never be completed: a national configuration does not know this district, as the model does not know this patient, and what the descent leaves undone is exactly the residue that education has to cover.   
 Five groups of actors are treated one by one — health professionals, social professionals, steering groups, community organisations, and citizens with their carers and intermediaries — each with the typical resources that its members must not lose, and each with the arrangements that would protect them.     
   
   The proposal is declared for what it is.   This document is an experiment produced with AI: the arrangements have not been tested, the groups of actors have not been consulted  ,   thirteen sections still await the author's judgement  , and every claim carries a reliability mark.      
   Widespread adoption of the document requires verification of its completeness, of the accuracy of its sources and of its internal coherence, including judgement on the sections that still carry the mark [CLAUDE], thirteen of them today.   
   Summary for the reader who has to decide 
 Each point summarises a chapter or a thematic block and closes with its own reliability mark and its principal source. 
 ●       Two educational questions are routinely merged into one, and the merger makes the harder of the two disappear : how to converse with these systems, which can largely be answered with a pedagogy that the caring professions already possess, and how to preserve the capacity to work without them, which no curriculum answers today {I, MDU-12 and this document, ch. 1}. 
 ●       The problem grows worse as the systems improve , because an unreliable system keeps vigilance alive whereas a reliable system removes the occasions for checking, and not checking a system that is almost always right is rational cognitive economy and not negligence {P, AIRA-KRIF-02a §1.2 and AIRA-HAL-04 A}. 
 ●       The machine is strong on exactness and is blind to pertinence and to feasibility , and it does not signal that it lacks the knowledge of the case on which pertinence depends; verification therefore migrates towards what is verifiable, and a badly designed educational programme certifies instead of protecting {I, AIRA-KRIF-02a §3.3}. 
 ●       The oracle position is a fact about the chain and not an attitude : whoever speaks last before the action is an oracle irrespective of their own accuracy, and a sceptical professional who acts on an output with nothing intervening downstream is treating it exactly as such {I, AIRA-KRIF-02a §1.1}. 
 ●       The pipeline that used to produce competence has been interrupted, and this is measured : unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4 to 22.4 per cent after continuous exposure to assistance, with converging findings in radiology and in pathology, while the occupational effect is a post that is never advertised rather than a dismissal, and is therefore invisible {T, Budzyń 2025; MDU-04}. 
 ●       The structure of the problem orients the solution, and a well-defined problem is already close to its solution because it supplies the criteria by which to judge it : formulating the question well is not a preliminary precaution but the greater part of the work, and it is for this reason that Chapter 4 opens from there instead of arriving at it in the end {L, maxim attributed to Einstein, an attribution that is widespread and has no ascertained source; this document, §4.1}. 
 ●       Conversing with these systems is a communication competence and not a technical competence , so what is needed is the deliberate transfer of an existing pedagogy plus compensation for three signals that a machine interlocutor does not give: it does not say that it lacks your context, it does not offer you resistance, and its fluency carries no information whatever about its confidence {I, this document, ch. 4}. 
 ●       The danger is not that the machine mirrors the starting position of the person asking, because it is also able to comment, to object and to show the holes in the reasoning ; the danger is that one has no way of knowing which of the two things one has received, given that elaborate confirmation and criticism arrive with the very same fluency, which is once again the third missing signal {I, this document, §4.1 and §4.2}. 
 ●       What is taught must be moves and not scripts , because a formulation repeated identically becomes liturgy, and prescribing four sentences to a profession produces exactly the lexical homogenisation that the document exists in order to prevent {I, AIRA-SKL-01 and MDU-13}. 
 ●       The five groups of actors differ by institutional defences and not by fragility, and each of them holds a resource that the machine does not have ; the question is not how to protect the weak but how to prevent each group from losing what it alone possesses {I, AIRA-HAL-10 §10.2}. 
 ●       A fifth group of actors is added here, the multi-stakeholder steering group , whose unit is not the person but the table, whose error manifests itself as distributed distortion visible only in aggregate, and which is the only group that has authority over the resources that all the other recommendations presuppose {I, KRIF-01a §3.1 and PAP-01 §6, extended here}. 
 ●       Tables fail in four ways, which here are no longer analytical distinctions but predictions each with its own observable : ratification, in which the output becomes the agenda and which is checked by counting how many alternatives appear in the minutes before a written proposal reaches the table; the prevalence of the lowest posture, which is checked by looking at who questions the material brought by someone else, and how many times; and the drift of the shared lexicon, which is checked by comparing, a year later, the glossary of the table with that of the system it uses {P, this document, §8.4}. 
 ●       The third and the fourth mode are the same failure seen twice , because sublimation without re-particularisation is the case in which the second movement does not occur, and what distinguishes the fault from correct functioning is precisely whether or not that movement is accomplished; the pair is not ours but is described in IAL-21, Chapter 2, as a bidirectional process performed by the artificial intelligence {L, single source and not independent}. 
 ●       Ratification has a pre-computational ancestor inside the corpus itself , the illusion of consensus described in IAL-21, in which participants believe they have agreed while they have merely found formulations that each of them interprets in their own way; it should therefore be presented as the amplified form of a failure already documented with no machine at all, whose antidote — AI as a systematic explorer of alternatives — simply remains inactive in ratification {L, IAL-21}. 
 ●       Ownership of the objective function is the non-delegable core , and it requires three instituted ingredients — a named holder, a calendar cadence, and a flow of data that measures the effects of the criterion rather than the functioning of the system; in their absence the "what counts" has been delegated to inertia {P, KRIF-01b §2.5 and §9.2}. 
 ●       What can be made invariant is to be built into the tool and what cannot belongs to education , and this is no longer an inference: a randomised study manipulated exactly this variable — same technology, same task, same students, the only difference being what was written in the system prompt — finding a fall of 17 per cent on the unassisted test in the arm without protections and a non-significant fall of 0.4 per cent in the protected arm {P, Bastani and colleagues 2024; this document, §12.2}. 
 ●       The sites of embedding are four and they form a cascade : the posture that sits in the generalist model, that is, asking before answering, declaring assumptions and not reassuring about what cannot be excluded; the supra-local reference configuration, national or international, produced as a public good for specific tasks and objectives; the local customisation of the instance, that is, this health district, these care pathways, these resources; and finally the loaded knowledge base, that is, the k-file, the glossary and the agreed core {P, this document, ch. 12}. 
 ●       The descent along the cascade cannot, however, be complete , because the limit set out in Chapter 2 holds for the configuration as well: a national configuration does not know this health district any more than the model knows this particular patient, and there always remains a residue to be configured locally and, beneath it, a residue that cannot be configured at all and is left to education {I, this document, §12.2}. 
 ●       The knowledge manager is not a sixth group of actors but a role internal to the steering group , because he or she has no institutional defence of their own and is rather the custodian of the resource of the fifth group, that is, of the knowledge distributed among the members and possessed by none of them, which the knowledge manager makes explicit, curates and loads into the tool {I, this document, §8.6}. 
 ●       The risk attaching to the knowledge manager is not the oracle but imitation without understanding , because he or she does not speak last and is not the only one to have seen, whereas the table may copy their formulations instead of learning their moves; the role is moreover transitory by design, with a sequence of led, co-led, autonomous, whose exit is to be dated in the initial mandate {I, this document, §8.6}. 
 ●       Seven arrangements constitute the educational equipment , and the three that have no current equivalent are those that answer the second question: seeded-error cases, recurrent practice without the system, and reconstructed apprenticeship {P on the evidence for the first two; MDU-09}. 
 ●       Education cannot supply time, mandate or staffing, nor can it heal the divergence between who pays and who benefits , and saying so openly is the defence against the use of education as an alibi in place of organisational change {I, MDU-09}. 
 ●       For four groups of actors time works in their favour, and this document will age into being the description of native functions; for citizens it works against them , because a system that is more fluent, warmer and more personalised aggravates the compensatory oracle, and the regulatory architecture presupposes the opposite {I, AIRA-HAL-08 K}.

title: Bevezetés a szerhasználó nők világába
text:
Bevezetés a szerhasználó nők világába. For many decades, the science of addictive behaviours focused on men, but since the 1990s, it has been recognized that gender differences are important for a more accurate understanding of addiction and for more effective treatment of girls and women who use drugs. In this volume, the characteristics of women and drug use are described in the light of the latest international and domestic research, as well as clinical practices. What do we know about women's substance use? In which theoretical models can it be interpreted? What treatments are effective? To what extent is the knowledge gained about women's substance use integrated into the treatment? What are the supporting and hindering factors for girls and women to receive treatment? To what extent are the knowledge gained about women's substance use valid in professional policy decisions? What other factors unrelated to drug use influence the knowledge, ideas, and attitudes of professionals and decision-makers? How does professional policy address intersectionality and diversity in the context of women's substance use?

It is worth discussing women's substance use by breaking it down into three major topics: theories, research and interventions. This triple structure is followed by this manual, which places female substance use in models and theories of addiction, presents the characteristics of female substance use, describes the results of a qualitative research conducted among pregnant substance-using women in Budapest, and summarizes the hallmarks of effective treatment and professional policy sensitive to female substance use.

Zsuzsa Kaló is an assistant professor at the Institute of Psychology at the Eötvös Loránd University of ELTE, a founding member of the ELTE Qualitative Psychology Research Group, president of the AKUT Foundation - for social integration, board member of the Hungarian Addiction Society, and plays an active role in many international professional organizations. Her main research areas are qualitative psychological studies, qualitative drug research, exploring the connections between women's trauma and drug use, as well as the topic of the use of new psychoactive drugs.

title: In vivo Study of the Effect of Composition and Implantation Site on Scaffold Degradation Rate: Poly(lactide-co-glycolide) 85:15+20wt%TaOx, Intraperitoneal
journal: Hix, Jeremy M.L., Troia, Arianna, Shapiro, Erik
text:
In vivo Study of the Effect of Composition and Implantation Site on Scaffold Degradation Rate: Poly(lactide-co-glycolide) 85:15+20wt%TaOx, Intraperitoneal.  Tissue engineering devices stabilize wounds, then degrade. However, published degradation rates often conflict. Incorporating monitoring functionality into devices allows real-time assessment of degradation and failure, but requires contrast agents, as polymer devices are invisible to most medical imaging modalities. Therefore, computed tomography (CT)-visible composite scaffolds were created from 5-20 wt% tantalum oxide (TaO x ) nanoparticles in polymers with distinct degradation profiles: polycaprolactone, poly(lactide-co-glycolide) (PLGA) 85:15 and PLGA 50:50, representing slow, medium and fast degrading materials. Scaffolds, mimicking biomedical devices, were implanted into mice intramuscularly or intraperitoneally, and monitored via CT over 20 weeks. Scaffold degradation profile was dictated by polymer matrix, regardless of nanoparticle addition. Foreign body response was dependent on implant site and in mid-degrading composites degradation rates transitioned from linear degradation intramuscularly to exponential degradation intraperitoneally. Nanoparticle excretion via liver and spleen lagged polymer degradation. Overall, real time tracking of device behavior was demonstrated, advancing an era of personalized medicine. Published as: Pawelec, K.M., Hix, J.M.L., Troia, A.  et al.  In vivo study of the effect of composition and implantation site on scaffold degradation rate.  Commun Mater  (2026). https://doi.org/10.1038/s43246-026-01308-5 
 This dataset contains longitudinal microCT scans of PLGA 85:15+20wt% TaOx, implanted intraperitoneally. Each individual in the group (n=6) was scanned 25 mm field of view (4 min total scan time) at 50 μm resolution, centered on the implanted scaffold. After all acquisitions, individual scaffolds were again sub-reconstructed using the Quantum GX software to 12 µm resolution.

title: Domby Sámuel: De vino Tokaiensi. A tokaji borról, 1758
journal: Pető, Gábor, N. Kis, Tímea, Molnár, Dávid
text: Domby Sámuel: De vino Tokaiensi. A tokaji borról, 1758. Sámuel Domby of Gálfalva (1729-1807) defended his doctoral dissertation "De vino Tokaiensi" at the University of Utrecht in 1758, which was published in the same year. The author not only summarised what was known about Tokaj wine, but also demonstrated through a series of medical and meteorological observations and chemical experiments why these wines were so excellent, what effects they had on a healthy human body and what ailments could be effectively treated by drinking them. In many respects, his work has stood the test of time: his observations on the importance of terroir and the protection of origin are still worth considering today.

title: Addiktológiai problémák Magyarországon. Helyzetkép a lakossági kutatások tükrében I. Szerhasználó magatartások
text:
Addiktológiai problémák Magyarországon. Helyzetkép a lakossági kutatások tükrében I. Szerhasználó magatartások. The National Survey on Addictive Problems in Hungary (NSAPH) 2019, which provides the primary background for the analyzes presented in the volume, is part of a series of targeted epidemiological studies that have been done for almost 20 years in Hungary. This study was aimed at examining various addiction problems and was striving for continuity as well as following international standards in terms of both methods and themes. In addition, the volume also relies on the data of the first wave of the Budapest Longitudinal Study (BLS) among young adults aged 18–34 in the capital in 2019, which thematically overlaps with the NSAPH 2019 study.

The aim of the NSAPH 2019 research is twofold. On the one hand, it deals with the prevalence of different addiction problems, while on the other, it deals with methodological issues related to the assessment of these behaviours. The main objective of the research is to examine the substance use related behaviours (drug use, alcohol consumption, smoking) as well as various behavioural addictions (problematic internet use, problematic social media use, problematic mobile phone use, video game use, problematic gambling, exercise addiction, work addiction, compulsive shopping/buying behaviour) of the Hungarian adult population, to identify the patterns of the different addiction problems based on social and psychological factors, and to describe the temporal and spatial location of the addiction data of the Hungarian general population. These objectives also appear in the structure of individual chapters of the volume. The goals for the development of the applied methodology are closely related to the final aim of the research as well, aimed at epidemiological estimation. One can read about them in more detail in the chapter dealing with the methodological background of the analyses in the volume, and the results obtained in this regard are primarily found in the chapter discussing the topic of drug consumption, which is particularly difficult to investigate with traditional tools due to social attitudes. In addition, the volume examines the social attitudes related to different substances/drug-using behaviours in a separate chapter, while another chapter deals with the relationship between the different addiction problems.

title: Data and code for: Circularity in automated ACMG variant classification
journal: ZHOU, Liangji, Chen, Yuanqiu, Chen, Tongtong
text:
Data and code for: Circularity in automated ACMG variant classification.  
 ## What is in the bundle, and what was deliberately kept out 
 
 | Path | Records | 
 |---|---| 
 | `data/erepo_reference_set.jsonl` | 9,653 | 
 | `data/erepo_nonsnv_resolved.jsonl` | 992 | 
 | `data/classifier_output.jsonl` | 9,343 | 
 | `data/erepo_curation_dates.json` | 12,950 | 
 | `data/clinvar_first_directional.json` + scan log | 6,436 | 
 | `data/clinvar_review_status.json` | 9,339 | 
 | `data/second_engine_subset.jsonl` + benchmark | 230 each | 
 | `data/tool_survey.json` | 13 tools | 
 | `scripts/` | 10 analysis + 3 display + 6 verification | 
 | `PREREGISTRATION_temporal_stratification.md` | - | 
 
 Every count above was checked against the number Data Availability states; the 
 script refuses to build if any disagrees. 
 
 **Kept out on purpose.** This repository is a clinical WES pipeline. It holds real 
 patient reports under `data/reports/` with patient names in the filenames, and a 
 patient database at `data/phenotype_cases.db`. The deposit is built from an 
 explicit allowlist, never a directory sweep, and a six-rule scan runs over the 
 staging tree before the archive is written. It refuses to package if anything 
 matches. A planted file named `chen_patient_report.xlsx` is used as the negative 
 control on every run and is detected. 
 
 **Field reduction.** `classifier_output.jsonl` drops `genebe_effects`, 
 `genebe_gene` and `genebe_n_gene_blocks`, keeping the applied criteria with their 
 strengths, the scores and the returned verdict. This is what Data Availability 
 says: "Redistribution of the classifier output is limited to the fields required 
 to reproduce the analysis." Anyone can regenerate the full response with 
 `scripts/fetch_genebe.py` and an API key. 
 
 ## One thing the file selection corrected 
 
 Data Availability says the deposit comprises "the expert-panel reference set 
 (9,653 records)". The file that name suggests, `data/eval/truthset_erepo.jsonl`, 
 holds **500** records; the 9,653-record extract is `data/eval/erepo_raw.jsonl`. 
 The staging script uses the latter and checks the count. Depositing the obvious 
 file would have contradicted the manuscript. 
 
 ## If you would rather not use Zenodo 
 
 Any repository that mints a DataCite DOI works and the manuscript wording does not 
 change. Figshare and Dryad both do. Zenodo is suggested because it reserves the 
 DOI before publication, which is what makes Step 3 possible, and because it is 
 free with no size negotiation at 1.0 MB. OSF does not reserve a DOI before 
 publication, which is why it is not suggested here.

title: IMPROVING THE APPLICATION OF INNOVATIVE AND SIMULATION-BASED METHODS IN TEACHING UROLOGY
journal: Sayfetdinov Sanjarbek Ikramiddin ugli, Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
text: IMPROVING THE APPLICATION OF INNOVATIVE AND SIMULATION-BASED METHODS IN TEACHING UROLOGY.  The rapid development of minimally invasive, endoscopic, laparoscopic, and robotic technologies has substantially changed the professional requirements of modern urologists. Traditional apprenticeship-based education alone is increasingly insufficient for providing trainees with repeated, standardized, and safe opportunities to develop complex procedural skills. Simulation-based education has therefore become an important component of contemporary urological training. The purpose of this study was to analyze current innovative and simulation-based approaches used in teaching urology and to identify practical strategies for improving their integration into medical education. A qualitative literature-based analysis was conducted using contemporary research on urological simulation, competency-based education, virtual reality, task trainers, three-dimensional models, surgical boot camps, and structured skills assessment. The findings indicate that simulation creates a controlled environment in which learners can repeatedly perform technical procedures without exposing patients to unnecessary risk. Virtual reality systems, endoscopic trainers, laparoscopic box trainers, robotic simulators, three-dimensional printed models, standardized patients, and scenario-based training can improve technical proficiency, procedural confidence, decision-making, and familiarity with urological instruments. However, the educational value of simulation depends not only on technological sophistication but also on curriculum design, deliberate practice, timely feedback, validated assessment, and integration with clinical experience. An effective model of urological education should combine theoretical instruction, simulation, objective competency assessment, supervised clinical practice, and repeated evaluation. Such an approach may improve training quality while promoting patient safety and supporting competency-based medical education.

text: Reproducibility package for "County-level wet-freezing weather and severe occupational same-level slipping reports in federal OSHA states: a time-stratified case-crossover study".  This reproducibility package accompanies a time-stratified case-crossover study of county-level wet-freezing weather and severe occupational same-level slipping reports in federal OSHA states. It contains the frozen protocol/statistical analysis plan and freeze evidence, protocol amendments, analysis and diagnostic code, synthetic estimator tests, source acquisition/checksum manifests, non-disclosive machine-readable aggregate result inventories, and manuscript table source files. The confirmatory protocol was frozen before injury dates were linked to case-day or referent-day weather and before any injury-weather effect was estimated or viewed. Raw third-party OSHA, Census, and NOAA files are not redistributed. OSHA narratives and exact coordinates, event-level spatial-linkage files, exact-coordinate frequency files, and event-linked matched county-day model inputs are also excluded; these materials can be reconstructed locally from the cited public sources using the archived code and checksums. The primary frozen analysis estimated an incidence rate ratio of 2.229 for severe same-level slipping reports on wet-freezing county-days, with interpretation constrained to wet-freezing episodes rather than an exact isolated-day causal effect.

title: PRiSM (Partial Responses in Structured Models): a Python framework for converting probabilistic binary classifiers into auditable nomograms
journal: Pigot, Henry, Lisboa, Paulo, Nilsson, Johan
text:
PRiSM (Partial Responses in Structured Models): a Python framework for converting probabilistic binary classifiers into auditable nomograms.  PRiSM (Partial Responses in Structured Models) is a model-agnostic framework that converts a trained probabilistic binary classifier for tabular data into a standalone nomogram that can be audited term by term. 
 PRiSM takes the shape of each nonlinear effect and interaction from the source model, not merely which variables mattered, and lets the observed outcome select and weight them. The result is an additive model that replaces the original classifier as the deployed predictor. Because the nomogram is additive on the log-odds scale, each variable's contribution can be read off and summed by hand. 
 This record archives the v0.1.0 source release. 
 Software authorship: the code archived here was written by Henry Pigot, Paulo J. G. Lisboa, and Johan Nilsson, and is released under the BSD 3-Clause License.

title: Glycosylation as a Universal Regulator of Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Target in Multifactorial Human Diseases
text: Glycosylation as a Universal Regulator of Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Target in Multifactorial Human Diseases.  Glycosylation is a fundamental molecular mechanism that integrates immune regulation, oncogenesis, inflammation, and pathogen interaction. Despite significant progress in understanding glycan biology, the clinical implementation of glycan-targeted strategies faces significant challenges due to the multifunctionality of glycans, their context-dependent nature, and methodological limitations. Overcoming these challenges requires the development of integrative platforms that combine glycomics with other omics disciplines, improved analysis methods, and the creation of more selective therapeutics. Glycobiology is one of the most promising areas of modern biomedicine, and further development of this discipline has the potential to revolutionize the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of many human diseases.

title: Post-Hoc Explainability for Contrastive Graph Anomaly Detection via Gradient Attention Maps
journal: Nekka, Iyad Assaad, SEBA, Hamida, Hidouci, Walid Khaled
text: Post-Hoc Explainability for Contrastive Graph Anomaly Detection via Gradient Attention Maps.  Graph anomaly detection on attributed networks has seen significant advances through deep learning, with contrastive self-supervised methods such as CoLA achieving stateof-the-art performance. However, these methods operate as black boxes: they flag nodes as anomalous without providing any explanation of which structural connections or feature dimensions drove that decision. In operational settings such as financial fraud detection, cybersecurity incident response, and clinical surveillance, a detection system that cannot explain its decisions is difficult to trust, audit, or act upon. In this paper, we introduce X-CoLA, the first post-hoc explainability framework for contrastive graph anomaly detection. X-CoLA integrates Gradient Attention Maps (GRAM) into the CoLA framework, applying a single backward pass through CoLA’s trained GCN backbone to produce node-level gradient attention maps that identify, for each flagged anomaly, which neighbors in the local subgraph and which feature dimensions of the target node drove the contrastive disagreement score. X-CoLA simultaneously distinguishes between structural anomalies, explained by high-gradient edges, and contextual anomalies, explained by high-gradient feature dimensions, without any modification to CoLA’s training procedure. We define three explainability metrics adapted to the contrastive setting: Gradient Fidelity, Structural Sufficiency, and Contextual Comprehensiveness. Experiments on the Cora benchmark dataset demonstrate that XCoLA achieves a Structural Sufficiency of 0.906 and a Gradient Fidelity of 0.602 while preserving CoLA’s detection AUC exactly. To the best of our knowledge, X-CoLA is the first work to apply post-hoc gradient-based explainability to a contrastive selfsupervised graph anomaly detection method.

Hypnose bei Epilepsie: Klinisches Potenzial einer adjuvanten psychophysiologischen Intervention.    Abstract   
  Epilepsie ist eine neurologische Erkrankung, deren Behandlung primär auf anfallssuppressiver Medikation sowie, bei entsprechender Indikation, chirurgischen oder neuromodulatorischen Verfahren beruht. Gleichzeitig beeinflussen Stress, Angst, Schlaf, Selbstwirksamkeit und psychosoziale Belastungen die Lebensqualität vieler Betroffener. Insbesondere wahrgenommener Stress kann bei einer Subgruppe zusätzlich mit dem individuellen Anfallsgeschehen assoziiert sein. Klinische Hypnose ist in diesem Zusammenhang als mögliche adjuvante psychophysiologische Intervention von Interesse. Eine spezifische antikonvulsive Wirkung ist bislang nicht hinreichend belegt. Demgegenüber zeigen Untersuchungen, dass Hypnose Aufmerksamkeits-, Stress- und autonome Regulationsprozesse modulieren kann. Parallel weisen systematische Übersichten darauf hin, dass psychologische, verhaltensbezogene und andere nichtpharmakologische Interventionen die medizinische Epilepsiebehandlung in ausgewählten Zielbereichen sinnvoll ergänzen können. Der vorliegende narrative Überblick diskutiert die klinische Rationale für Hypnose bei Epilepsie mit Schwerpunkt auf Stressregulation, Anfallsangst, Selbstwirksamkeit und Selbsthypnose sowie auf Sicherheitsaspekten und Forschungsbedarf.

title: Processed ECG-derived SKNA and sequential replay data during intermittent negative airway pressure in a porcine model
journal: Rahmani, Shahrokh, Hertel, Julie Norup, Linz, Benedikt
text:
Processed ECG-derived SKNA and sequential replay data during intermittent negative airway pressure in a porcine model.  This dataset accompanies the manuscript “A Reproducible Event-Driven Analytical Framework for ECG-Derived Skin Sympathetic Nerve Activity Analysis: Towards Afferent Signal Processing for Closed-loop Neuromodulation.” 
 The dataset provides processed data and analytical outputs supporting a reproducible event-driven framework for the analysis of electrocardiogram-derived skin sympathetic nerve activity (ECG-derived SKNA) during intermittent negative airway pressure (INAP) in anaesthetised, spontaneously breathing pigs. 
 The main development cohort comprises 50 porcine INAP recordings. The release includes processed ECG-derived SKNA signals, gold-standard INAP event annotations, recording-specific adaptive burst thresholds, event-centred SKNA and burst-occupancy results, and deployment-oriented sequential replay outputs. ECG-derived SKNA was obtained from available ECG channels using high-frequency filtering, rectification, artefact handling, 1-s moving-average smoothing, median fusion across available channels, and downsampling of the resulting SKNA envelope to 100 Hz. Missing or unusable ECG channels were excluded rather than imputed. 
 Recording-specific adaptive burst thresholds were defined as the maximum of three baseline-derived candidate thresholds: the intersection of a two-component Gaussian mixture model (GMM), the baseline 95th percentile, and the baseline median + 6×median absolute deviation (MAD). The deployment-oriented sequential replay used a 30-s trailing analysis window, 10-s updates, a >5% burst-occupancy criterion, and persistence for two consecutive qualifying updates. 
 The release additionally contains processed signal, event-metric, and replay outputs from a separate multi-event recording used to evaluate the prespecified analytical pipeline without further parameter adjustment. 
 A continuous intervention proof-of-principle recording is also provided. This recording contains four 75-s INAP events, with two occurring before and two during dorsal root ganglion (DRG) stimulation at 4 Hz and 0.3 mA. These data demonstrate the continuous, sequential application of the framework through an experimental recording before and during an intervention. This recording was not designed or analysed to assess the efficacy of DRG stimulation and should not be interpreted as a treatment comparison. 
 The dataset is accompanied by three software resources supporting the analytical and deployment workflow: 
 SKNA Event-Driven Framework: ECG-derived SKNA processing, adaptive burst detection, event-centred analysis, and sequential replay. SKNA Cohort Explorer : interactive exploration and visualisation of recording-level and cohort-level SKNA analytical outputs. SKNA Deployment Monitor: deployment-oriented sequential SKNA analysis, burst-occupancy monitoring, and persistence-gated trigger simulation. 
 Versioned releases of these software resources are archived separately on Zenodo and are linked to this dataset through the record's Related works metadata. 
 The public release is intended to support processed-data-level reproducibility and reuse.  
 The repository includes a comprehensive README and data dictionary describing the dataset organisation, variables, analysis outputs, units and reuse conventions.

title: Intensivkapazitäten und COVID-19-Intensivbettenbelegung in Deutschland
text: Intensivkapazitäten und COVID-19-Intensivbettenbelegung in Deutschland.  Der Datensatz "Intensivkapazitäten und COVID-19-Intensivbettenbelegung in Deutschland" des Robert Koch-Instituts dokumentiert die tägliche intensivmedizinische Versorgungslage seit der COVID-19-Pandemie. Basierend auf Meldungen aller intensivbettenführenden Krankenhäuser in Deutschland erfasst das DIVI-Intensivregister Echtzeitdaten zu belegten und freien Intensivbetten. Die Erhebung differenziert nach Altersgruppen, Regionen und Versorgungsstufen. COVID-19-Fälle auf Intensivstationen werden gesondert ausgewiesen. Die Daten stehen aggregiert auf Bundes-, Landes- und Kreisebene zur Verfügung. Damit bildet der Datensatz eine Grundlage für die Überwachung von Kapazitäten, die Koordination von Behandlungskapazitäten und politische Entscheidungsprozesse während der Pandemie und darüber hinaus.

title: PRISMA-ScR checklist for Muscle ultrasound for the assessment of myosteatosis and muscle quality across the lifespan, with emphasis on paediatric metabolic risk: a scoping review protocol
journal: Puelles-Díaz, Alvaro, García-Leal, Héctor, González-Aroca, Joaquín
text: PRISMA-ScR checklist for Muscle ultrasound for the assessment of myosteatosis and muscle quality across the lifespan, with emphasis on paediatric metabolic risk: a scoping review protocol.  Myosteatosis, the infiltration of skeletal muscle by fat, has been studied predominantly in the context of ageing, sarcopenia and functional decline, yet emerging evidence suggests that altered muscle quality may emerge earlier in the life course, particularly among paediatric populations with metabolic risk. Muscle ultrasound is an accessible, non-ionising, portable alternative to computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging, but its use is methodologically heterogeneous and the biological construct represented by echo intensity remains uncertain. This scoping review aims to map the available evidence on the use of muscle ultrasound to assess myosteatosis and muscle quality across the lifespan, with emphasis on paediatric populations with metabolic risk, and to characterise methodological heterogeneity, analysis and normalisation strategies, the biological validity of ultrasound-derived parameters, and knowledge gaps. The review will follow the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and will be reported using the PRISMA-ScR guidance. Studies of children, adolescents and adults, whether healthy or with metabolic, neuromuscular, neurodegenerative or functional conditions, will be eligible when they report at least one ultrasound-derived measure interpreted as muscle fat infiltration, muscle composition or muscle quality. MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, SPORTDiscus, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library will be searched, together with grey-literature sources and citation searching. References will be managed in Zotero; two reviewers will screen records independently and in duplicate in Rayyan; and data will be charted in a piloted spreadsheet using a verified single-extraction model. Findings will be presented using descriptive numerical analysis, narrative summaries, tables and evidence maps; no meta-analysis and no formal risk-of-bias assessment will be undertaken. The review will provide the first lifespan map of muscle ultrasound for myosteatosis and muscle quality, with particular relevance for resource-limited and Latin American settings.
